name: Ecommerce Website Reference
summary: Full ecommerce storefront reference with catalog, inventory, cart, checkout, orders, payments, shipping, returns, SEO and marketing measurement.
intent: Build a custom-coded storefront while keeping transactional behavior governed by NEXT F Commerce schemas, rules, APIs, permissions, events and integrations.
flows: Cart → Checkout → server-side Commerce Rules → Order
Payment provider callback → validated adapter → Payment state → canonical Event
Purchase/refund business fact → canonical event → consent-aware marketing/analytics mapping
securityBoundaries: Customer domain and hosting remain customer-owned and are not NEXT F platform services.
Customer-editable content remains separate from developer-controlled presentation and source code.
Public website clients may read only published public data through approved API/runtime paths.
Secrets, OAuth tokens, payment credentials and webhook signing secrets remain server-side.
Organization/Site authorization is rechecked server-side; a Site ID in browser input never grants access.
Optional analytics/marketing destinations respect the canonical consent state and environment binding.
Canonical permissions, Events, APIs and Connectors are reused rather than recreated inside the customer project.
Preview/staging/production identities and integrations remain isolated.
Browser-submitted price, tax, discount, inventory, payment and refundable values are never authoritative.
Raw payment card PAN/CVV storage is prohibited; payment providers remain behind trusted adapters.
antiPatterns: Do not trust browser price/tax/discount/inventory values
Do not merge payment and fulfillment status
Do not let product edits rewrite historical Orders
Do not implement subscriptions/bookings/gift cards until dedicated contracts are enabled
acceptance: nextf.site.json validates and pins the exact Contract Version.
All enabled Modules exist in the Module Registry and all required dependencies resolve.
All selected Capabilities belong to enabled Modules and are not reserved/unsupported.
Customer-editable data maps to canonical schemas rather than hardcoded presentation values.
Public API usage exposes only permitted published/public projections.
Protected CMS/Admin actions map to canonical permissions and are re-authorized server-side.
Standard Events and tracking names are used without project-local synonyms.
Configured integrations use canonical Connectors and preserve consent/environment rules.
No secrets are present in nextf.site.json, public bundles, example payloads or public logs.
Codex reports actual verification results and any deviations/extensions before handoff.
The implementation includes only the Site-specific page/content architecture required for the Ecommerce Website Reference and does not convert contracts into a generic page builder.
CMS navigation is derived from enabled Modules/Capabilities and filtered by canonical permissions.
NEXT F Admin retains internal diagnostics/configuration boundaries that are not exposed as customer privileges.
All money, inventory, checkout, payment, refund and fulfillment mutations enforce Phase 12 Commerce Rules on trusted server boundaries.
Order/Payment/Fulfillment historical facts are snapshot-safe and cannot be rewritten by later catalog edits.

codexHandoff.instruction: Build the customer-specific Ecommerce Website Reference presentation against NEXT F Contracts 0.23.0. Treat the example as a reference contract composition, not a visual template. Reuse the exact Manifest, Module, Schema, API, Permission, Event, Webhook and Integration identifiers. Do not invent parallel NEXT F architecture. Report deviations and missing canonical coverage before implementing those paths.

sourceNotes: Reference examples are architecture/composition examples, not customer branding or visual templates.
Provider integrations shown as optional remain customer-owned accounts and must be explicitly configured.
A reference example can be reduced or extended only through the canonical Module/Capability and Contract Extension rules.
